channel.title: ChatGPT & Codex changelog
channel.description: Latest updates to ChatGPT and Codex.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- Open a CSV file to preview it as a table. Select **View source** to edit it in the same tab. - When you open another Markdown file, the editor remembers whether you last used source or preview.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- On Windows, branch reviews now count changed files and lines correctly when many files have long paths. - Fixed an issue that prevented some HTML files with large embedded images or videos from opening in preview.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- Open a ZIP file in the file viewer to browse its folders and preview files such as PDFs and images without extracting them.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- The November 20 update fixed an issue where recent activity could disappear from a long local chat while Codex was still working.

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- Side chats are now saved on compatible paired computers, so you can reopen them later from the original task. - The new project picker lets you choose Cloud or select a paired computer and project when starting a task. - Toggle word wrap for individual code blocks and diffs in a task. - Start a new Codex task with <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd> N </kbd> on iPad.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- The subagent indicator counts only agents that are still working or waiting. Open **Subagents** from the task menu to revisit finished agents and see which model and reasoning level each used. - Task search dismisses the keyboard when you open a result. Collapsed task list sections stay collapsed on iPhone. - Fixed the composer becoming unresponsive after opening a task from a completion notification. - Fixed transcripts jumping when reopening a task or returning to the app, and crashes when scrolling past or expanding inline videos. - Follow-ups no longer get stuck in the queue because an earlier turn still appears active. - Unsaved annotation text survives when you return to the app. Creating a worktree now preserves untracked files with names that include accented letters or quotation marks.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in Work and Codex
item.description: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in Work and Codex
item.content:encoded:
# GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in Work and Codex
GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Choose Astra for your hardest projects, such as implementing and testing a change across an existing codebase or turning a report into slides that follow your template. Choose Sol for everyday coding, writing, and multistep workflows. With GPT-6.2 Sol, you can complete more tasks on the same paid plan than with GPT-6.1 Sol.
Pro $200 subscribers can use GPT-6.2 Sol in Ultrafast mode. Pro $500 subscribers can use Ultrafast with both GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra. See [Models](/codex/models#recommended-models) for help choosing a model and [Speed](/codex/agent-configuration/speed#gpt-62-speed-options) for plan and workspace requirements. Read the [release announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-2-astra-sol/) for more details.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- The November 17 update added a fork option to the title menu for local chats. In a Git project, you can also fork the chat into a new worktree. - The November 18 update added [GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra](/codex/changelog#codex-gpt-62-astra) to the model picker for Amazon Bedrock in supported AWS Regions.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- Fixed a formatting issue where a price such as `$5/month` and part of a later link could appear as math if the link contained a dollar sign. - Copying part of a formatted response now preserves links, list numbering, and checked boxes when you paste it into a rich-text editor. - Restored **Edit plugin** when you reopen an installed private workspace plugin from **Personal** > **Created by you**.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- When you reopen the app after a quit or crash, Codex now automatically resumes eligible local chats. The chat must still be interrupted, have been active in the past 24 hours, and belong to the same ChatGPT account you're using.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- Fixed an issue where switching accounts could make local projects, remote projects, and pinned tasks disappear from the sidebar. - When you comment on a passage in Pages, the comment box now keeps focus as you type and attaches your comment to the selected text. - Replies now render inline equations enclosed in single dollar signs, such as `$x + y$`, and keep prices such as `$5 each` as text next to an equation.

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- Paste images and files into the full-screen composer, and open file attachments from sent prompts. - Switch between drives in the folder picker on Windows hosts. - Dictate annotation notes. - Hide the task list on iPhone Duo without leaving the current task.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- Reopening a running Codex Cloud task keeps loaded messages visible. - Sent prompts stay above their replies, even when the host confirms receipt late. - Expanded command cards show the full command and more of its output. - Improved keyboard and toolbar behavior on iPad and iPhone Duo. - Fixed opening changed files and loading response images on Windows hosts. The folder picker now opens on Linux hosts that can't locate a home folder. - Manual pairing works with VoiceOver and on devices that can't scan QR codes.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- On macOS and Windows, the home screen loads faster, the first response in an existing chat appears sooner, and PDF previews and code reviews open faster. - Fixed an issue on macOS where the integrated terminal could display non-ASCII characters incorrectly when the app started without a language setting. - The November 8 update made the **Send**, **Queue**, and **Steer** buttons appear dimmed when they're unavailable.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- Codex can now use controls in the in-app browser that require holding down a key.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- When you search a chat or PDF, the Find bar now waits for the search to finish before reporting zero results.

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- Add, preview, and remove attachments without leaving the full-screen composer. - Task read status now syncs with supported hosts, helping clear stale unread indicators across devices.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- Follow-ups steer the running task by default unless you have saved a different preference. - Improved response annotations: add and edit notes on selected text, and tap numbered references to revisit the selected text and its note. - Custom-provider tasks keep their model and reasoning effort when you send a follow-up from iOS. - When you reopen a task, prompts that failed to send retain their attachments, and you can retry sending them. - Improved keyboard behavior when opening tasks, scrolling long drafts, and returning to an open editor. - Drafts, text selection, and undo history survive changes between compact and split layouts. - Improved iPhone Duo layouts, including full-width editing and controls that stay above the keyboard. - Linked files open directly, and closing the preview takes you back to the task. Absolute file links outside the workspace also open correctly. - Images with relative file paths load from the directory where the original turn ran. - Fixed invisible chart labels and bars in inline visualizations. - Reconnect errors show a single Retry control, with better alignment on iPad. - Archiving a task can reconnect to its host when the computer appears offline.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### New features
- On Windows, shortcuts to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\chatgpt-desktop.exe` now keep working after an app update. - In the October 31 update, Codex offered **Resume** or **Keep paused** when you reopened the app after a quit or crash. The prompt covered interrupted local chats active in the past 24 hours if you were signed in with the same ChatGPT account.
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- If switching Git branches fails, Codex now restores which changes were staged and which were unstaged.

item.title: Codex app
item.content:encoded:
# Codex app
### Performance improvements and bug fixes
- When you steer Codex while it's responding, the chat now keeps the interrupted reply above your message and shows the revised reply below it. - Selecting a code review finding now takes you to the correct line and keeps it in view as the diff loads.

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- Play audio and video directly in responses. - Tap a sub-agent's name in task activity to open its conversation.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- Draft attachments and annotations are now restored when you reopen a task or restart the app. - Reference autocomplete supports chat and skill names containing spaces. Plugin skill names are also easier to read. - Plan mode preserves your selected reasoning effort when using the same model. - Loaded activity stays visible if loading older work times out, with an option to retry. - Queue-loading failures now offer a Retry action. - Improved support for Windows file links and Markdown images. - Fixed worktree creation on Linux hosts. - Fixed crashes when steering queued messages or editing pairing codes, and iPad freezes when switching or resizing tasks.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra in Work and Codex
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra in Work and Codex
item.content:encoded:
# GPT-6.1 Terra in Work and Codex
GPT-6.1 Terra is now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans. It's a fast, efficient model for professional work that combines strong image understanding with precise computer use.
Reason about images and screens, then act on what you find across your browser, desktop, and apps. Terra also provides clear, direct writing that puts results first and explains supporting details in plain language.
Choose GPT-6.1 Terra from the model list in **Advanced** in the ChatGPT desktop app or ChatGPT Work on the web. Work also supports Terra on mobile. The model isn't available in Chat and does not support UAE inference residency. Enterprise access depends on workspace availability and administrator controls.
See [Models](/codex/models?surface=app#app-gpt-61-terra) for guidance and [browser use](/codex/browser) and [computer use](/codex/computer-use) for tool setup and access requirements.

item.title: Codex app

# Codex app

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- View and stop background commands using the new pill above the composer on supported remote hosts. - Mention chats from other connected hosts with `@`.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- A loading indicator now shows when saved messages are refreshing. - Activity groups are cleaner, and you can open images inspected by Codex on demand. - Unanswered questions remain available after a turn finishes and when reopening a chat. - More reliable replies to questions while another prompt is starting or finishing. - Autocomplete suggestions appear as each source loads, without waiting for slower sources. - Usage-limit explanations and reset times now appear directly in the chat. - Fixed prompts incorrectly appearing to fail after a response timeout. - Fixed extra lines in diffs after repeated edits to the same file. - Images in responses open in the full-screen gallery, and attachment removal targets the correct image. - The voice button returns after a call ends, so you can start another without reopening the chat.

item.title: Codex app

- On case-sensitive file systems, dragging files such as `Report.txt` and `report.txt` into a chat now attaches both in the order you dropped them. - The October 21 update fixed an issue that could prevent a chat from starting in a new worktree.

item.title: Codex app

### Performance improvements and bug fixes

item.title: GPT-5.5 retirement in Codex
item.content:encoded:
# GPT-5.5 retirement in Codex
Effective October 14, 2026, at noon PDT (19:00 UTC), GPT-5.5 retires from Codex for users signed in with ChatGPT. The OpenAI API and Codex sessions authenticated with an API key aren't affected.
Use **GPT-6.1 Sol** (`gpt-6.1-sol`) when available to your plan and client. Update workspace defaults, saved model settings, managed configurations, custom agents, scheduled tasks, and scripts that still select `gpt-5.5`.
See [GPT-5.5 retirement](/codex/models#gpt-55-retirement) for plan-specific replacements and [workspace model availability](/codex/enterprise/workspace-model-availability#prepare-for-the-gpt-55-retirement) for administrator guidance.

item.title: ChatGPT for iOS
item.content:encoded:
# ChatGPT for iOS
### New features
- File citations now open directly in the file viewer. - Collapse the entire Projects section to reach recent tasks faster.
### Improvements and bug fixes
- Faster task and thread loading, with saved task names and recent messages visible while reconnecting. - Markdown now renders in sent prompts, with questions quoted above your replies. - Queued messages appear immediately, with more reliable handling during turn interruptions. - Markdown files open in rendered view by default. - Clearer skill names and improved autocomplete after punctuation. - Fixed missing Rename prompts and usage percentages on iPad. - Plan mode stays selected when returning to the task list. - Custom permission mode now respects project-defined permissions. - Improved task widget reliability, including when local authentication is enabled for Codex. - Usage widgets adapt to accounts with only a weekly limit. - Connection errors offer a Retry action without hiding saved messages. - Fixed raw image URLs appearing in image-only messages.

item.title: Composer predictions in Codex
item.content:encoded:
# Composer predictions in Codex
Composer predictions adds autocomplete-style suggestions for your next message in the Codex desktop app. After Codex responds, it uses the current conversation to suggest a follow-up prompt in the message box. Press **Tab** to accept the suggestion as an editable draft, or type your own message. Accepting a prediction doesn't send it for you.
The feature is available in beta to users aged 18 and older with personal ChatGPT Pro plans in supported regions, in local and SSH threads with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
Learn more about [composer predictions](/codex/features/composer-predictions).

item.title: Linux desktop preview and agent imports
item.description: Install ChatGPT on Linux, import existing agent setup, and keep desktop imports up to date.
item.content:encoded:
# Linux desktop preview and agent imports
### Install the ChatGPT desktop app on Linux
The [ChatGPT desktop app for Linux](/codex/linux/linux-app) is available in preview for supported Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora desktop distributions on x64 and ARM64 processors. Download the `.deb` or `.rpm` package for your distribution, then sign in to work with projects, local files, and Codex.
### Import setup and recent work from other agents
The desktop app supports **Claude Code**, **Claude Cowork**, and **Cursor**. [Import instructions, settings, skills, plugins, projects, and recent work](/codex/import), then turn on automatic updates in **Settings > Import** to keep imported work in sync.
Codex CLI can also import supported setup and recent chats from Claude Code and Cursor with `/import`.

# GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.2 deprecated
GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.2 are now deprecated as user-selectable models in Codex for users signed in with ChatGPT. API-key workflows aren't affected.
Use a current Codex model, such as GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, or GPT-5.4 mini. See [Codex models](/codex/models#deprecated-codex-models) for model availability and [Codex pricing](/codex/pricing#credits-overview) for credit rates.

item.title: Build and install plugins in Codex
item.description: Build and install plugins in Codex
item.content:encoded: # Build and install plugins in Codex Codex now supports **plugins**: installable bundles that package skills, app integrations, and MCP server configuration for reusable workflows. Plugins are available in the Codex app, CLI, and IDE extensions. You can install curated plugins from the plugin directory, or scaffold a local plugin with `@plugin-creator` and test it with workspace-scoped or home-scoped marketplaces. Learn more in the [plugins documentation](/codex/plugins). #### Plugin structure Every plugin is a folder with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest and optional supporting files: ```text my-plugin/ .codex-plugin/ plugin.json # Required: plugin manifest skills/ # Optional: packaged skills .app.json # Optional: app or connector mappings .mcp.json # Optional: MCP server configuration assets/ # Optional: icons, logos, screenshots ``` #### Install plugins per-user or per-repo You can install plugins for just yourself with `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and `~/.codex/plugins/`, or for everyone on a project with `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and a repo-local plugin directory such as `./plugins/`. #### Curated plugins and local development Codex surfaces curated public plugins in the plugin directory. Codex also ships with the built-in `@plugin-creator` skill to help you scaffold a plugin, add a local marketplace entry, and test it before sharing it with teammates.

item.title: Introducing GPT-5-Codex-Mini
item.content:encoded:
# Introducing GPT-5-Codex-Mini
Today we are introducing a new `gpt-5-codex-mini` model option to Codex CLI and the IDE Extension. The model is a smaller, more cost-effective, but less capable version of `gpt-5-codex` that provides approximately 4x more usage as part of your ChatGPT subscription.
Starting today, the CLI and IDE Extension will automatically suggest switching to `gpt-5-codex-mini` when you reach 90% of your 5-hour usage limit, to help you work longer without interruptions.
You can try the model for a new Codex CLI session using:
```bash codex --model gpt-5-codex-mini ```
You can also use the `/model` slash command in the CLI. In the Codex IDE Extension you can select GPT-5-Codex-Mini from the dropdown menu.
Alternatively, you can change your default model to `gpt-5-codex-mini` by updating your `config.toml` [configuration file](/codex/local-config):
```toml model = "gpt-5-codex-mini” ```
